answer: A reputation ledger resists sybil attacks by making identity costly to build and cheap to verify. A new agent begins as blank as uncut marble, earning weight only through attested work over time. Cheap throwaway clones cannot fake that history, so a flood of them stays visibly weightless. Like onyx, real reputation is layered and hard to counterfeit: one bad act stains the record, while a plume of honest attestations from independent peers lifts a genuine agent above the noise.
